svg.title: CE conformity flow under the Machinery Regulation
svg.text: CE conformity flow – Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC until 19 Jan 2027, Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 from 20 Jan 2027
Four cases in this project. The person in the lane header is the "manufacturer" who signs the declaration. Annex numbers refer to Regulation 2023/1230.
APC, test bench, AGV, run-in rig – you = manufacturer
HMC, robot cell, AS/RS – you = user
robot arm, linear unit, spindle unit
FMS cell, line; APC added to HMC
C-standard first, then A/B; EMC, RoHS, PED/SPVD, RED
hazard list, risk estimation, PLr per safety function
ISO 13849-2, PE / insulation tests, stopping times
user language; digital allowed (paper on request)
Annex I? see box right; else Module A (Annex VI)
Annex IV Part A; keep 10 years after last unit
Annex V Part A; CE on nameplate; put into service
B1 Check CE plate + EU DoC
language, schematics, PL summary, stop times
AGV transfer, robot loading → lane D
Annex XI; + relevant docs Annex IV Part B
from step 3: you are manufacturer of the result
common job · common control · hazard transfer
new hazard / higher risk, safety control changed
D5 File + EU DoC for assembly
single machines keep their own CE
D6 CE plate for the assembly
Step 7 – which conformity procedure? (Regulation 2023/1230, Art. 25 + Annex I)
e.g. removable transmission devices, vehicle servicing lifts, ML-based safety components
notified body always: B + C, H or G
e.g. presses with manual loading, logic units, person-detecting devices
Module A only if harmonised standards fully applied
HMC with own APC, test bench, AGV, rotary-table station
Module A – internal production control (Annex VI)
machines put into service up to 19 Jan 2027
Annex IV list (23 types) with the same logic
• Date rule: a machine placed on the market or put into service from 20 Jan 2027 (also own-built for own use) follows Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 – no transition.
• Harmonised standards listed under 2006/42/EC do not automatically give presumption under the Regulation – check the new OJEU / Commission lists.
• Technical documentation: risk assessment, drawings, calculations, test reports, standards list, instructions, DoC; safety software logic on reasoned request.
• Cyber: Annex III 1.1.9 "protection against corruption" – document network access, passwords, IEC 62443 measures for safety-related controls.
• UK (GB): Supply of Machinery (Safety) Regulations 2008 – UKCA, CE currently accepted (check). Northern Ireland follows EU law.
• A Declaration of Incorporation is never enough for a complete machine – ask for an EU Declaration of Conformity.
EXAMPLE – check the current edition of every standard
